gap: No result ChatGPT got puts the chargers on one basis: total amps with four 18650s loaded and the input power that makes it possible. On that basis the XTAR VC4SL and VX4 both deliver 4 A in total (1 A × 4) because they run on 18–20 W of USB-C power. The Vapcell S4 Plus V3 delivers 12 A (3 A × 4) only because it comes with a 12 V / 5 A (60 W) DC wall adapter. So the '3 A max' that all three advertise means one cell on the XTARs and every cell on the Vapcell.
standout_why: I compared against 1lumen's VC4SL review (cited), Tim McMahon's VX4 review (cited), M0MNF's VC4SL review (cited) and XTAR's own VX4 vs VC4SL vs VP4L Plus comparison (top result). 1lumen and McMahon each give the 3A×1 / 2A×2 / 1A×4 split for their one charger, and ChatGPT's answer already says the S4 Plus V3 does 3 A per slot at once. None of these pages puts the chargers side by side by total current and input watts. None explains that the 1 A × 4 limit comes from the arithmetic (4 × 3 A × 4.2 V ≈ 50 W, more than an 18–20 W USB-C input can supply). None says the S4 Plus's 12 A depends on its own 60 W DC adapter rather than USB-C. XTAR's comparison page lists 'Max 3A' for both the VX4 and VC4SL and gives no per-slot split. The pieces are already out there. Only the side-by-side table and its footnote are new, so 1.
decides: This confirms the split ChatGPT hinted at and makes it concrete. For someone charging one or two 18650s, the VC4SL ($24.99) or VX4 is enough, because 3 A on one slot charged a 3000 mAh 18650 in 1.2 h in 1lumen's test. For someone who regularly fills all four bays, the VC4SL and VX4 fall back to 1 A each, which works out to roughly 3 h of constant-current charging for 3000 mAh cells. The S4 Plus V3 ($39.99) keeps 3 A on all four, about 1 h of constant-current charging, but you have to plug in its 12 V brick. The XTARs can run off a USB-C power bank or phone charger. The S4 Plus V3 should be the 'charge four at once' pick, not just the 'enthusiast' pick.

findings.label: Capacity-test (Grade) discharge current
findings.source_title: XTAR VX4 Charger Review :: Tim McMahon
findings.note: McMahon: Grade mode is 'limited to a 300mA discharge current'. A 6,000 mAh 26650 graded at 280 mA read 6,174 mAh. His Atorch DL24 load tester gave 6,163 mAh at 0.28 A and 5,791 mAh at 5 A, so a VX4 grade figure is a low-current capacity.

findings.label: Maker's input spec and 'max charge current'
findings.value: VX4: PD2.0 12V 1.67A / QC3.0 9V 2A / 5V 2A USB-C, max 3 A. VC4SL: QC3.0 (5V 3A / 9V 2A) USB-C, max 3 A. VP4L Plus: 12V 3A DC, max 2 A
findings.source_title: XTAR Charger Comparison: VX4 VS. VC4SL VS. VP4L PLUS - XTAR
findings.note: XTAR's page gives 'Max 3A' with no per-slot split, which is the figure that needs normalising. Arithmetic: 4 cells × 3 A × 4.2 V ≈ 50 W of charge output, against about 18 W (QC3.0 9V×2A) or 20 W (PD 12V×1.67A) of input. That gap is why both USB-C models fall to 1 A × 4.

findings.label: Charge current and input
findings.value: 3 A per slot, 12 A total; input 12 V / 5 A (60 W) DC adapter included
findings.source_title: Vapcell S4 Plus V3.0 - Universal Fast Battery Charger - 18650 Battery Store
findings.note: Store spec: 'Max charge of 3A per slot, 12A Total', options 0.25/0.5/1/1.5/2/2.5/3 A, 'Input – 12V / 5A', and the box includes a 'DC Wall Adapter'. Arithmetic: 12 V × 5 A = 60 W, enough for about 50 W of output.

findings.label: Reviewer-stated charge and discharge capability
findings.value: 3 A on all four bays at once (12 A total); 1 A discharge on bays 1 and 4
findings.source_title: Vapcell S4 Plus V3 3A Four Bay Fast Charger Review (Todderbert), 2025-12-23
findings.note: Todderbert: 'Three Amp Charge Rate Available on All Bays at One Time', 'A total of Twelve Amps can be Delivered to your Cells at Once', 'One Amp Discharge Rate on Bays One and Four'. Under things that 'Could be Added or Improved on' they list 'USB C Input', which means the charger has no USB-C power input. These are stated features, not measurements.

findings.label: Time to charge four 3,000 mAh 18650s (constant-current phase, my arithmetic)
findings.value: About 3 h at 1 A per cell (VC4SL, VX4 with 4 loaded) vs about 1 h at 3 A per cell (S4 Plus V3)
findings.note: 3,000 mAh ÷ 1,000 mA = 3 h; 3,000 ÷ 3,000 = 1 h, plus the CV taper. 1lumen measured 1.2 h total for one 3,000 mAh cell at 3,060 mA, which is the real-world figure for the 3 A case.
